review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

16:1.sourceText: Περὶ δὲ τῆς λογίας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους, ὥσπερ διέταξα ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Γαλατίας, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιήσατε.
16:1.targetText: Now about the collection for the saints, you are to do as I directed the churches of Galatia:

groups.note: Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
οὕτως ("so") is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB has no word for καί ("also") here.

16:2.sourceText: κατὰ μίαν σαββάτου ἕκαστος ὑμῶν παρ’ ἑαυτῷ τιθέτω θησαυρίζων ὅ τι ἐὰν εὐοδῶται, ἵνα μὴ ὅταν ἔλθω τότε λογίαι γίνωνται.
16:2.targetText: On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside a portion of his income, saving it up, so that when I come no collections will be needed.

groups.note: Distributive κατά ("by, each") with the accusative is rendered On … every.
The feminine μίαν ("one") implies ἡμέραν and is rendered as the ordinal the first.
παρ’ ἑαυτῷ ("by himself") is rendered aside with set.
The clause ὅ τι ἐὰν εὐοδῶται ("whatever he may prosper in") is rendered a portion of his income; BSB's Greek differs slightly here, with the same sense.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
γίνωνται ("take place") is rendered will be needed.

unmappedSource.reason: τότε ("then") is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the noun day that the feminine μίαν implies; N1904 has no word for it.
English supplies an object for saving.

16:3.sourceText: ὅταν δὲ παραγένωμαι, οὓς ἐὰν δοκιμάσητε, δι’ ἐπιστολῶν τούτους πέμψω ἀπενεγκεῖν τὴν χάριν ὑμῶν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ·
16:3.targetText: Then, on my arrival, I will send letters with those you recommend to carry your gift to Jerusalem.

groups.note: ὅταν ("when") is rendered on with the noun arrival.
The verb παραγένωμαι ("I arrive") is rendered as a noun, my arrival.

unmappedSource.reason: The relative οὓς ἐάν ("whomever") is left unexpressed in English; τούτους supplies those.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:4.sourceText: ἐὰν δὲ ἄξιον ᾖ τοῦ κἀμὲ πορεύεσθαι, σὺν ἐμοὶ πορεύσονται.
16:4.targetText: And if it is advisable for me to go also, they can travel with me.

groups.note: The articular infinitive τοῦ … πορεύεσθαι is rendered to go.
κἀμέ ("me also"), the subject of the infinitive, is rendered for me … also.

16:5.sourceText: Ἐλεύσομαι δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὅταν Μακεδονίαν διέλθω· Μακεδονίαν γὰρ διέρχομαι,
16:5.targetText: After I go through Macedonia, however, I will come to you; for I will be going through Macedonia.

groups.note: ὅταν ("when") with the aorist is rendered After.

16:6.sourceText: πρὸς ὑμᾶς δὲ τυχὸν καταμενῶ ἢ καὶ παραχειμάσω, ἵνα ὑμεῖς με προπέμψητε οὗ ἐὰν πορεύωμαι.
16:6.targetText: Perhaps I will stay with you awhile, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has a different verb here with the same meaning, stay.
προπέμψητε ("send on") is rendered help … on my journey.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

16:7.sourceText: οὐ θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἄρτι ἐν παρόδῳ ἰδεῖν· ἐλπίζω γὰρ χρόνον τινὰ ἐπιμεῖναι πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ Κύριος ἐπιτρέψῃ.
16:7.targetText: For I do not want to see you now only in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.

unmappedSource.reason: The second γάρ is not separately expressed; BSB joins the clauses with a semicolon.

16:8.sourceText: ἐπιμενῶ δὲ ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἕως τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς·
16:8.targetText: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:9.sourceText: θύρα γάρ μοι ἀνέῳγεν μεγάλη καὶ ἐνεργής, καὶ ἀντικείμενοι πολλοί.
16:9.targetText: because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me.

groups.note: The adjective ἐνεργής ("effective") is rendered for effective work.
καί ("and") is rendered even though.
The participle ἀντικείμενοι ("opponents") is rendered oppose.

unmappedSource.reason: καί ("and") joining great and effective is absorbed into BSB's for effective work.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for oppose.

16:10.sourceText: Ἐὰν δὲ ἔλθῃ Τιμόθεος, βλέπετε ἵνα ἀφόβως γένηται πρὸς ὑμᾶς· τὸ γὰρ ἔργον Κυρίου ἐργάζεται ὡς κἀγώ·
16:10.targetText: If Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.

groups.note: The adverb ἀφόβως ("without fear") is rendered nothing to fear.
γένηται ("he may be") is rendered he has … while he is.
BSB resumes ἐργάζεται ("he is doing") with am.
κἀγώ ("I also") is rendered I.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a conjunction to split the clause.

16:11.sourceText: μή τις οὖν αὐτὸν ἐξουθενήσῃ. προπέμψατε δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν εἰρήνῃ, ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρός με· ἐκδέχομαι γὰρ αὐτὸν μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.
16:11.targetText: No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he can return to me, for I am expecting him along with the brothers.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

16:12.sourceText: Περὶ δὲ Ἀπολλῶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ, πολλὰ παρεκάλεσα αὐτὸν ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν· καὶ πάντως οὐκ ἦν θέλημα ἵνα νῦν ἔλθῃ, ἐλεύσεται δὲ ὅταν εὐκαιρήσῃ.
16:12.targetText: Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was not at all inclined to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity.

groups.note: The article serves as the possessive our.
πολλά ("much") is rendered strongly.
θέλημα ("will, desire") is rendered inclined.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB has no word for καί here; it begins a new sentence.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies Apollos as subject; the Greek subject is θέλημα ("will").

16:13.sourceText: Γρηγορεῖτε, στήκετε ἐν τῇ πίστει, ἀνδρίζεσθε, κραταιοῦσθε.
16:13.targetText: Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.

groups.note: The third-person imperative γινέσθω ("let … be done") is rendered as the command Do.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts "let all your things be done" as a command to you, so ὑμῶν ("your") has no separate word.

16:15.sourceText: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί· οἴδατε τὴν οἰκίαν Στεφανᾶ, ὅτι ἐστὶν ἀπαρχὴ τῆς Ἀχαΐας καὶ εἰς διακονίαν τοῖς ἁγίοις ἔταξαν ἑαυτούς·
16:15.targetText: You know that Stephanas and his household were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints. Now I urge you, brothers,

groups.note: The article serves as the possessive his.
ἀπαρχή ("firstfruits") is rendered the first converts.
The genitive Ἀχαΐας ("of Achaia") is rendered in Achaia.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English recasts the household of Stephanas as Stephanas and his household.

16:16.sourceText: ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ὑποτάσσησθε τοῖς τοιούτοις καὶ παντὶ τῷ συνεργοῦντι καὶ κοπιῶντι.
16:16.targetText: to submit to such as these, and to every fellow worker and laborer.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB has no word for καί ("also") here.
ὑμεῖς ("you") is not repeated here; BSB's I urge you in verse 15 already names them.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:17.sourceText: χαίρω δὲ ἐπὶ τῇ παρουσίᾳ Στεφανᾶ καὶ Φορτουνάτου καὶ Ἀχαϊκοῦ, ὅτι τὸ ὑμέτερον ὑστέρημα οὗτοι ἀνεπλήρωσαν·
16:17.targetText: I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived, because they have supplied what was lacking from you.

groups.note: ἐπί ("at") with the noun παρουσίᾳ is rendered as a that-clause.
The noun παρουσίᾳ ("coming") is rendered as a verb, have arrived.
τὸ ὑστέρημα ("the lack") is rendered what was lacking.
The possessive ὑμέτερον ("your") is rendered from you.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
καί ("and") between Stephanas and Fortunatus is shown by a comma in English.

16:18.sourceText: ἀνέπαυσαν γὰρ τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα καὶ τὸ ὑμῶν. ἐπιγινώσκετε οὖν τοὺς τοιούτους.
16:18.targetText: For they refreshed my spirit and yours as well. Show your appreciation, therefore, to such men.

groups.note: τὸ ὑμῶν ("the [spirit] of you") is rendered yours.
ἐπιγινώσκετε ("recognize") is rendered Show your appreciation.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:19.sourceText: Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῆς Ἀσίας. ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἐν Κυρίῳ πολλὰ Ἀκύλας καὶ Πρίσκα σὺν τῇ κατ’ οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίᾳ.
16:19.targetText: The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings.  Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets at their house.

groups.note: The genitive Ἀσίας ("of Asia") is rendered in … Asia.
BSB resumes ἀσπάζεται ("greets") with so does for the church.
σύν ("with") is rendered and.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds that Asia was a Roman province.
English supplies a relative clause for κατ’ οἶκον ("at the house").

16:20.sourceText: ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες. Ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ.
16:20.targetText: All the brothers here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the place word here.

16:21.sourceText: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου.
16:21.targetText: This greeting is in my own hand—Paul.

groups.note: The article with the greeting is rendered This.
The dative article and χειρί ("hand") together supply in … hand.
The possessive ἐμῇ ("my") is rendered my own.

16:22.sourceText: εἴ τις οὐ φιλεῖ τὸν Κύριον, ἤτω ἀνάθεμα. μαρὰν ἀθά.
16:22.targetText: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be under a curse. Come, O Lord!

groups.note: BSB renders this Aramaic phrase, written differently in BSB's Greek text, as the prayer Come, O Lord.

16:23.sourceText: ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ μεθ’ ὑμῶν.
16:23.targetText: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.

16:24.sourceText: ἡ ἀγάπη μου μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
16:24.targetText: My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus.  Amen.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.
